manuscript_edits.quote: [Observed] What the rebuilt negative actually says. Every one of the 23 pfk13 codons is fixed at the reference residue, with a single N458D call giving codon 458 a reference frequency of 0.999. Two qualifications the previous version did not make. The denominator is per codon and runs from 1,845 to 1,876 of the 1,900 isolates, not 1,900 at every codon, so "all 1,900 isolates" was never the right phrase. And the isolates were collected between 2009 and 2021, which makes this a historical negative: it is evidence about the sampling period and carries no information about the present. The negative is now stronger in substance — it covers the complete validated set, including the three validated markers the old results never reported, and it reports the two candidates that had been misclassified as validated — and weaker in the form it may be stated in.

manuscript_edits.concept: Explicit count in already qualified fixed-codon exception
manuscript_edits.quote: [Observed] The pfk13 panel was rebuilt from the WHO molecular-marker compendium v1.0 (December 2025) rather than from memory. It now covers all 14 validated markers — F446I, N458Y, C469Y, M476I, Y493H, G533S, R539T, I543T, P553L, R561H, P574L, C580Y, R622I, A675V — and all 6 candidates — E252Q, P441L, C469F, N537I, G538V, V568G. That is 14 + 6 = 20 variants at 19 distinct codons, because C469Y (validated) and C469F (candidate) are two different changes at the same codon 469; the two WHO tiers are kept distinct throughout and no candidate is anywhere described as validated. Four further pfk13 codons (449, 481, 515, 527) fall outside both lists, which is why the reconstruction covers more codons than the lists contain: 23 pfk13 codons in total, and every one is fixed at the 3D7 reference residue, with the single exception of codon 458, where one isolate in 1,866 carries Asn458Asp. The validated residue at that codon is Tyr, which is absent.
